text:
maya: Heads up — Acme reported their console showing negative tokens/sec and TTFT drops for their streaming route in eu-west-1 starting ~09:12 UTC. Screenshot attached: https://files.acme.example/neg-tokens.png

alerts-bot: [ALERT] stream-metrics-rollup: tokens/sec negative delta detected for customer=acme (eu-west-1) — 5 occurrences in last 2m

jonah: Can you paste a quick repro or the raw metric query you used? Also which model/route?

maya: Route = /v1/streams/generate (streaming), model variant = redwood-v2-8k. Quick PromQL we used in the console (rolled-up series):
```
sum by(customer,region) (increase(redwood_streaming_tokens_total{route="/v1/streams/generate"}[5m])) / 300
```
This produced small negative values (-0.4 to -120 tokens/sec) for several 1m windows.

ingrid: Negative increases usually mean a counter reset or out-of-order delivery to the rollup job. Do we have Kafka consumer lag/rewind events around 09:10-09:14?

maya: We checked; there was a consumer rebalance at 09:11 due to an autoscaler pod restart (node drain). Offset rewind logs attached (snippet):
```
[09:11:03] consumer: rebalance - assigned partitions: 12
[09:11:04] consumer: commit failed - OffsetOutOfRangeError - seeking to earliest
[09:11:05] consumer: start reading from 0 (rewind)
```
We think the rollup saw older offsets and applied them causing negative deltas.

jonah: That makes sense. Two pathways: (1) rollup should detect non-monotonic counter and clamp to 0 for deltas, (2) we need to avoid double-ingesting the same batch when consumer rewinds. Which rollup worker handled eu-west?

maya: eu-west rollup pod id = rollup-eu-3. Logs show it processed the same partition range twice after the rebalance.

on-thread note by oncall-matt (added): @oncall-matt taking this one. Temporary mitigation: pause rollup-eu-3 ingestion to stop further negative ticks, and backfill correct aggregates.

oncall-matt: Quick steps I'll run:
1) pause ingestion via feature flag: `rollup.ingest.eu-west=false`
2) run aggregation backfill job with dedupe by (partition,offset) and clamp negative deltas to 0
3) restart rollup with commit-check enabled

lina-billing: Customer is asking if this will affect billing invoice for the month. If tokens/sec goes negative on dashboard, does that impact metering?

jonah: Good question — billing uses raw events upstream of rollup (billing_pipeline), not the console rollup. Negative dps shouldn't affect billing, but confirm: billing pipeline consumer had no rewind.

maya: Confirmed — billing_pipeline logs show no rewind or errors. Lina, billing shouldn't be affected but I'll ping billing infra for double-check.

ingrid: Root cause action items:
- fix rollup to clamp negative increases (safe guard)
- make rollup idempotent when reading rewound partitions (dedupe on partition+offset)
- add alert suppression for expected rebalance windows and improve runbook
- backfill script to rebuild eu-west 09:10-09:20 window

jonah: For telemetry/forensics we should also capture these artifacts:
- rollup-eu-3 raw ingestion log (09:00-09:30)
- kafka controller logs for rebalance event
- consumer offsets and commit history
- backfill diff report (before vs after)

maya: Repro steps for eng to validate locally:
1) run local kafka with topic partition producing monotonic counter `tokens_total`
2) produce values 100, 200, 300 (normal)
3) simulate rewind by producing older offsets with lower total (50) to same partition
4) run rollup binary and observe negative `increase()` output in 1m windows
(Example producer snippet):
```bash
# normal sequence
echo '{"offset":1,"tokens_total":100}' | kafkacat -P -t streaming-metrics
echo '{"offset":2,"tokens_total":200}' | kafkacat -P -t streaming-metrics
# rewind event (older offset replayed)
echo '{"offset":1,"tokens_total":50}' | kafkacat -P -t streaming-metrics
```

oncall-matt: I'll run the pause + backfill now. Putting a quick temporary console banner: "We are investigating intermittent negative tokens/sec metrics in eu-west; billing not impacted."

lina-billing: Thanks — please @mention me when backfill completes so I can confirm with the customer.

maya: I'll attach the screenshots and logs to the ticket (ACME-4521) and update the customer thread.

jonah: For the code fix I'll open a PR with two changes: clamp delta >= 0, and add consumer dedupe cache keyed by (topic,partition,offset-range) with TTL. Will request review from @ingrid.

ingrid: Sounds good. After backfill, monitor TTFT and tokens/sec for 2 hours and close incident if stable.

maya: Thanks team :thumbsup:
